sections.heading: Our Jamii — the communities we serve
sections.lead: "Jamii" is Swahili for community, or family. It is who CECF works for: the grassroots groups and the people behind them, across every county we reach.
facts: Every group gets a public page
Receipts sent straight to the donor's phone

sections.heading: A page for every community we work with
prose: Every group we register gets a public Jamii page — who they are, what they are raising for, and a receipt for every shilling given, sent straight to the donor's phone. It is how the communities in our network tell their own story, and how supporters find and back them directly.
Jamii is not only for the groups already inside our formal registration programme. Any community group — a chama, a youth collective, a self-help group — can start a page and be discovered.

media.alt: Institutions connected around a community group

sections.heading: The communities in our Jamii
sections.lead: CECF's registration and referral work reaches a wide range of groups. These are the communities we most often support.

items.title: MSMEs & grassroots groups
items.body: Chamas, table-banking groups, cooperatives and small enterprises moving from informal to formally recognised.

items.title: Women's groups
items.body: Women-led savings, trading and enterprise groups building financial independence together.

items.title: Youth groups & enterprises
items.body: Young people organising around skills, enterprise and community projects.

items.title: Gender & GBV support groups
items.body: Groups providing peer support, referral and advocacy around gender-based violence and gender equity.

items.title: Vulnerable & marginalised communities
items.body: Groups supporting members facing poverty, displacement or social exclusion, connected to the services they need.

items.title: Refugees & displaced persons
items.body: Refugee-led and host-community groups working toward recognition, livelihoods and belonging.

items.title: Persons with disabilities
items.body: Groups led by and for persons with disabilities, formalising to access services and opportunity on equal terms.

items.title: Older persons & elders
items.body: Elder-support and intergenerational groups — core to CECF's own mission alongside child welfare.

sections.heading: Care doesn't stop at registration
prose: CECF's own name comes from the two groups our founders started with: children and elders. Every community on this list — MSMEs, women's and youth groups, refugees, persons with disabilities — is that same idea applied wider: people organising to look after each other, formally recognised so the systems around them can help too.
ticks: A public page for every registered group
Direct, receipted support from anyone, anywhere
Referral into banking, government and donor services

sections.heading: See the impact. Support a community.
sections.body: Every community we work with has a Jamii page of their own. Browse them to see the impact they are having, start a page for your own group, or register with CECF to begin the formalisation journey.
